breaking-news-scan.md.scenario: A digital-asset desk runs a mid-morning breaking-news scan across crypto markets, stablecoins, and digital-asset regulation from a pasted batch of overnight wire items.
fills: Crypto markets, stablecoins, and digital-asset regulation.
Moves a major-asset price by more than about 3 percent, changes a rule or its published timeline, or affects a tracked entity (a major exchange, a top-two USD stablecoin issuer, or a G20 regulator).

Raw wire items and headlines pulled this morning (all fictional and illustrative; entities and figures are synthetic). Timestamps are ET on 2026-07-10 unless noted.
1. 08:52 — Regulator publishes final examination guidance for bank use of payment stablecoins; effective in 90 days. (Primary: regulator newsroom.)
2. 08:40 — Bitcoin down 4.2 percent overnight to a two-week low on broad risk-off; Ether down 5.1 percent. (Market data wire.)
3. 08:15 — Meridian Digital Exchange confirms it paused withdrawals of one low-cap token after detecting anomalous contract activity; customer funds 'unaffected'. (Exchange statement.)
4. 07:58 — A mid-cap USD stablecoin ('the fourth-largest') briefly traded to 0.984 in Asian hours before recovering; issuer cites a temporary redemption backlog. (Two wires, one issuer note.)
5. 07:30 — EU authority opens a consultation on extending MiCA reporting thresholds; comment period 60 days. (Primary: authority notice.)
6. Yesterday 18:00 — Opinion column argues stablecoins will 'replace correspondent banking'. (Op-ed, no new fact.)
7. 06:40 — Layer-2 network Harbor Rollup reports record daily stablecoin settlement volume of 9.1 billion dollars. (Network dashboard + one wire.)
8. 05:20 — Unconfirmed forum chatter that a top-two exchange faces a regulatory probe; no named source. (Social, unverified.)
9. Two days ago — Recap of last week's rate decision. (Stale rehash.)
10. 08:05 — A large asset manager files to launch a tokenized money-market fund on a public chain. (Primary: filing.)
11. 07:10 — Cross-chain bridge Aurelia halts operations after a suspected signer-key compromise; estimated 22 million dollars at risk, under investigation. (Bridge status page + two wires.)
12. 06:00 — Minor protocol announces a routine version upgrade with no user impact. (Project blog.)
None — first run; baseline. No prior scan to diff against; nothing to drop as already-reported.

committee-reporting-pack.md.scenario: A committee secretariat assembles the June 2026 pack for Harborview Financial Group's monthly Financial Crime Risk Committee from pasted metrics, notable items, and a prior-action log.
fills: The monthly Financial Crime Risk Committee of Harborview Financial Group — governance oversight of BSA/AML, sanctions, and fraud risk across the bank, including the digital-asset advisory line.

Columns are metric | current | prior | threshold/appetite; all illustrative and internal to this scenario.
1. Open SAR/STR investigations | 214 | 176 | appetite <= 180
2. Average SAR filing age (days) | 41 | 33 | limit <= 30
3. Sanctions screening alerts generated | 12,930 | 11,410 | no fixed limit (volume KRI)
4. Sanctions alert false-positive rate | 96.1% | 95.8% | target <= 95%
5. True-match sanctions hits escalated | 7 | 4 | all must be escalated (target 100%)
6. KYC/CDD refresh backlog (accounts) | 1,380 | 1,510 | appetite <= 1,200
7. High-risk customer periodic reviews overdue | 62 | 58 | limit 0
8. Transaction-monitoring alerts closed within SLA | 88% | 91% | target >= 90%
9. Screening-system uptime | 99.2% | 99.9% | target >= 99.9%
10. Training completion (financial-crime, staff) | 97% | 96% | target >= 95%
11. Adverse-media alerts pending review | 240 | 205 | appetite <= 200
12. Digital-asset (stablecoin/on-chain) alerts | 58 | 31 | new KRI, no threshold set yet

All items illustrative and internal to this scenario.
- 2026-06-14: Sanctions screening system suffered a 6-hour outage during a vendor update; alerts queued and were cleared by 2026-06-15 with no confirmed missed screening, but the incident breached the 99.9 percent uptime target and is subject to a post-incident review.
- June: SAR filing age and open-investigation count both moved adversely, driven by two analyst departures and a spike in fraud alerts; the backlog pushed average filing age past the 30-day limit.
- 2026-06-22: Internal audit issued a finding that the digital-asset transaction-monitoring rules lack documented thresholds and tuning evidence (rated Medium).
- 2026-06-09: A sanctions-list update was applied within the required window; one true-match hit was identified, escalated, and the relationship exited.
- Emerging risk: stablecoin/on-chain alert volume nearly doubled month over month as a client pilot went live, against a KRI that has no calibrated threshold.

Columns are action | owner type | due | status note; all illustrative.
1. Recruit two additional AML investigators | HR / Financial Crime | 2026-06-30 | one offer accepted, one role still open
2. Reduce SAR filing age below limit | Financial Crime Ops | 2026-05-31 | not achieved; age rose to 41 days
3. Complete sanctions screening tuning to lower false positives | Sanctions team | 2026-07-15 | on track, tuning in test
4. Document digital-asset monitoring thresholds | Digital-Asset Advisory | 2026-06-15 | overdue; work not started, owner cited competing pilot demands
5. Vendor change-management review after prior minor outage | Technology | 2026-05-15 | overdue; not closed before the 2026-06-14 outage recurred
6. Clear KYC/CDD refresh backlog below appetite | Onboarding Ops | 2026-08-31 | on track; backlog fell to 1,380

8. Refresh high-risk customer review procedure | Policy | 2026-07-31 | on track

(1) Approve incremental funding to complete sanctions screening-system resilience work (redundant failover) following the June outage. weekly-roundup.md.scenario: A chief-of-staff analyst closes out the week across a personal research-and-tooling program of four active workstreams, grading the week and setting next week's priorities.
fills: a personal research-and-tooling program of four active workstreams: a market-intelligence dashboard, a compliance typology library, an on-chain monitoring tool, and a betting-analytics model

The week's source material (all fictional and illustrative; week of 2026-07-06 to 2026-07-10):
- Mon 07-06: market-intelligence dashboard shipped a new regulatory-tracker tab; on-chain tool had a false-positive spike (12 spurious alerts) traced to a mislabeled address list.
- Tue 07-07: compliance typology library added 2 new typologies (stablecoin de-peg exploitation, bridge signer-key compromise); betting-analytics model backtest completed on last season's data.
- Wed 07-08: on-chain tool address-list fix deployed; false positives dropped to near zero. Dashboard latency issue reported by no users but noted internally.
- Thu 07-09: betting-analytics model produced its first live-week edges (3 flagged, average projected edge 6 percent); typology library update entered review.
- Fri 07-10: market sell-off (Bitcoin -4.2 percent) surfaced a data-refresh gap in the dashboard during high volume; bridge halt (Aurelia) auto-flagged by the on-chain tool as intended.
Metrics this week: dashboard uptime 99.4 percent; on-chain alert precision recovered from 71 percent (Mon) to 98 percent (Fri); typology library at 17 total entries; betting model backtest ROI +4.1 percent, hit rate 54 percent.

Metrics export and log notes (illustrative): dashboard weekly active views 210; on-chain tool processed about 41,000 transactions and raised 63 alerts (58 true after the fix); typology library review queue has 1 item pending; betting model flagged 3 edges, none yet settled. Blocker log: dashboard data-refresh gap under load is unresolved; one typology entry is awaiting a regulatory-citation check.
None — first run; baseline. No prior roundup to anchor the week-over-week comparison or the scorecard trend line.
